claims.text: TestProcessDetectors.setUp is a no-op override that only calls super().setUp(), a leftover remnant from merging StatefulDetectorHandlerTestMixin into BaseDetectorHandlerTest.
Is MetricAlertDetectorHandler being left as `pass` a deliberate placeholder (pending a future stateful implementation), or was it an oversight when the base class was changed?
Docstring says this returns a list of DetectorEvaluationResult, but the method now returns a dict keyed by DetectorGroupKey. Consider updating the docstring to match the new return type.
build_handler's detector_type parameter is never passed by any of its ten call sites in the file, making it a dead/unused parameter left over from the test refactor.
Mutable class attribute counter_names should be annotated with typing.ClassVar

The test helper parameter name `type` in create_detector_and_conditions shadows the builtin `type`, and reads awkwardly since `type` in this codebase is also a Detector field name and a GroupType concept.

build_mock_occurrence_and_event hardcodes the same id for every call, and IssueOccurrence.__eq__ only compares by id, so all occurrences from this helper compare as equal regardless of fingerprint or group_key, making multi-group test assertions unable to distinguish between occurrences for different groups
This expected occurrence is built with the wrong group key/value, so the test can pass without validating the new hook inputs.

Was removing the duplicate-group-key detection and its logger.error call a deliberate transfer of responsibility to each handler, or just incidental cleanup once the return type became a dict? If deliberate, is the new "keys must be unique and match result.group_key" contract documented anywhere?
On line 196, the expected occurrence for group_2 is built with value=6 when the data packet has group_2=10 - this only passes because value is never used in occurrence construction

The occurrence is sent to Kafka before commit_state_updates() runs; if the commit fails, will the next data packet re-produce the same occurrence (a duplicate issue) rather than just a duplicate resolve as before?

The `import builtins` / `builtins.type[GroupType]` workaround (needed because the Detector model has a field literally named `type`, which shadows the builtin inside the class body) is correct but has no explanatory comment, making it likely a future "cleanup" will revert it back to `type[GroupType]` and break CI again.
Inconsistent value parameter in test: data packet specifies {"group_1": 6, "group_2": 10} but build_mock_occurrence_and_event for group_2 is called with value=6 instead of value=10

MetricAlertDetectorHandler inherits from StatefulDetectorHandler but only contains pass, failing to implement its required abstract methods: counter_names (property), get_dedupe_value(), get_group_key_values(), and build_occurrence_and_event_data(). This will cause a TypeError at runtime when the class is instantiated.
Unused value parameter in build_mock_occurrence_and_event helper function

The new test assertions on IssueOccurrence are effectively empty: IssueOccurrence.__eq__ only compares `id`, and the test helper build_mock_occurrence_and_event hardcodes the same id string for every occurrence it builds, so any two occurrences produced by the helper compare equal regardless of fingerprint, group_key, priority, or other content — meaning this PR's main new assertions verify nothing, as demonstrated by two tests whose expected values already don't match what's actually produced yet still pass.

Detector.project_id is still hardcoded to return 1; now that this change wires up actually producing and sending IssueOccurrence to Kafka, what mechanism prevents occurrences from being written against project 1 before a real project_id is added to the model?

In test_state_results_multi_group, the second occurrence is built with value=6 even though group_2 has a value of 10 in the data packet, so the test won't catch regressions in how value is threaded into build_occurrence_and_event_data
This assertion allows extra Kafka publishes, so the test no longer catches duplicate occurrence production.
A TODO comment ("This will be a stateful detector when we build that abstraction") describing work that this very PR completed was left in place instead of being removed.

TestEvaluateGroupKeyValue.test_dedupe passes wrong group key ('val1') to build_mock_occurrence_and_event, causing fingerprint mismatch with the key ('group_key') passed to evaluate_group_key_value, breaking the assertion
